title: Top K Frequent
description: Count frequencies in a Map, then keep the K most frequent. Sort + slice is the readable baseline; a size-K min-heap is the O(n log k) upgrade.

notes: Step 1 is always the same: build a frequency Map in one O(n) pass.
Sort DESCENDING by count: (a, b) => b[1] - a[1]. Reversing the operands gives ascending.
For O(n log k), push each entry into a min-heap of size K and pop when it overflows — keeps only the top K alive.
Bucket sort by frequency is the third option: O(n) overall, but uses O(n) extra buckets.

questions.q: Why a Map for frequencies instead of a plain object?
options: Maps allow numeric keys without string coercion and iterate in insertion order

questions.q: Which comparator sorts entries by count DESCENDING?
Time complexity of the sort-then-slice approach?
How does a min-heap of size K give O(n log k)?
options: For each of n entries we push and possibly pop (both O(log k)), keeping only the top K alive
It does not — it is also O(n log n)

exercises.prompt: Fill in the count-and-sort Top K. The comparator direction is the trick.

blanks.hint: second operand of the descending subtraction

L3.prompt: Write `topKFrequent(nums, k)` returning the K most-frequent values. Log `JSON.stringify(topKFrequent([1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3], 2))`.
hints: Count first, sort second, slice third.
For O(n log k), swap the sort for a size-K min-heap keyed by frequency.
